clue.text: Perhaps it's Johnson's way of speaking to poor Ray

parts.note: diction is a person's manner of speaking or enunciating

indicators.note: poor suggests the word Ray is in a bad, broken state, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the way Dr Johnson talks to a down-at-heel man called Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' turns RAY into ARY, added after DICTION. Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 Dictionary of the English Language, hence 'Perhaps it's Johnson's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Johnson's great work was a lexicon of English, so 'perhaps' it is his famous book.

clue.text: But this Cambridge Professor did not create Fantasia

definitions.text: But this Cambridge Professor did not create Fantasia

parts.words: But this Cambridge Professor did not create Fantasia
parts.note: Cambridge has a professorship of archaeology named after John ..., its founder, who shares a surname with the maker of the 1940 cartoon film

explanation.walkthrough: The Disney Professorship of Archaeology at Cambridge bears John Disney's name; Walt Disney made the animated film Fantasia.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to a Cambridge chair's founder and to the Hollywood animator.

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number
William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: A title shared by numerous senior churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' is the definition, not part of a description of archbishops.
explanation.definitionFit: Claud is a man's first name.

clue.text: Advantage of one variety of net over others

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first pieces are placed above the next

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: a variety of the word net is another form of it, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the rest means the others

explanation.surface: One kind of net has a benefit over other kinds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' turns NET into NTE; 'over' stacks I and NTE above REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake or benefit in something is an interest in it, as in 'in your interest'.

definitions.meaning: Alfred ... was an English poet, author of The Highwayman
someone undecided says '...', wavering between refusal and agreement

explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Noyes's surname, said as NO-YES, is what a doubtful person answers.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the poet Alfred Noyes also reads as a hesitant reply, both refusal and assent.

parts.note: a candle made from the pith of a marsh plant dipped in fat; 'in a hurry' plays on that plant's name meaning haste

explanation.walkthrough: The cheap candle was made from the pith of a marsh plant; its name also means a lamp grabbed in haste.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush light is a primitive candle made from a dipped plant stem.

parts.note: a parrot is traditionally called ... or ..., and a survey that gathers people's opinions shares the name, so the bird is 'opinionated'

explanation.surface: An exasperated owner complains about a pet bird with strong views.
explanation.walkthrough: Poll is a stock name for a pet parrot, and an opinion survey is also a poll: the bird is 'opinionated' because its name is a canvass of opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses meet: the traditional pet-parrot name and a survey of public opinion.

parts.note: doing as you are told is a virtue, and one of the vows taken by those entering holy orders

explanation.walkthrough: 'taking orders' means both obeying commands and becoming a monk or priest, whose vows include this virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Submission to commands is a virtue and a monastic vow.

definitions.meaning: someone who tunes in to the wireless

explanation.definitionFit: The Listener was a BBC weekly, and a person who tunes in to broadcasts hears them.

clue.text: See a large number before the poet

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal

explanation.surface: A large crowd turns up to see a poet perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' only invites the solver to look; it gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy.

clue.text: Dark type is bashful about excrescence

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the word for bashful goes round the growth

parts.note: bashful means shy
a wart is a small growth or excrescence on the skin

explanation.surface: A timid, dark-complexioned person is self-conscious about a skin blemish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts WART inside SHY. 'type is' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarthy complexion is a dark, dusky one.

definitions.meaning: gulls that fly over the coast
a cat mews, so a 'catfish' in the ocean would make ocean mews: the cries tell you one is there

explanation.definitionFit: Sea mews are gulls; read as 'sea' plus 'mews', it is the sound of a cat living in the ocean.

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
der is German for 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone sorts trees into kinds native to other countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The foreign types' means more than one foreign word for 'the': Spanish EL and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree or shrub with white flowers and dark berries.

definitions.meaning: a card or peg game played by one person alone
a single gem set alone and shown off in a finger ring

explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire names both a one-player pastime and a lone gemstone mounted by itself in jewellery.

clue.text: See attendant about crime in building

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the attendant's word surrounds the crime

parts.note: a page is a boy attendant or servant
arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property

explanation.surface: A bishop's assistant investigates an offence committed in a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ARSON inside PAGE. 'See' is a church word (a bishop's diocese) that suits the surface but here only leads into the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsonage is the house provided for a parish clergyman to live in.

definitions.meaning: an older sense: a disease or disorder of the body

explanation.definitionFit: The word means fondness and also, in medical use, a bodily disorder.

clue.text: No welcome to the visitor (who may find you out ?)

definitions.text: No welcome to the visitor (who may find you out ?)

parts.words: No welcome to the visitor (who may find you out ?)
parts.note: a servant tells an unwanted caller the householder is unavailable; 'find you out' means both discover you absent and see through you

explanation.walkthrough: The polite fiction of telling callers you are away from home; the visitor 'finds you out' in both senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the standard excuse given to callers one did not wish to receive.

clue.text: Taking the part of a certain gentle churchman

indicators.note: taking part of the following words means the letters lie inside them, across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone plays the role of a mild-mannered clergyman in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'certaIN GEntle'. W. R. Inge, the 'gloomy Dean' of St Paul's Cathedral, London, was a well-known churchman and writer of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean William Inge was a famous Anglican clergyman, so he is an example of a churchman.

definitions.meaning: migrating birds that arrive in Britain for the warm months

explanation.definitionFit: Swallows means gulps down, and the birds are migrants arriving for the warm season.

definitions.meaning: an NCO rank in the army
the word describes bodily punishment such as caning, so it sometimes accompanies 'punishment'

explanation.definitionFit: It is a junior army rank and also the adjective for physical punishment, as in 'corporal punishment'.

parts.note: fifty per cent is a half and superior means better, giving the fond phrase for a spouse, 'better half'

explanation.surface: Something claims to be half again as good as its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Fifty per cent' as 'half' and 'superior' as 'better': 'better half' is the jocular name for one's married partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A husband's 'better half' is his spouse, in the idiom.

clue.text: Posted instead to make a change

indicators.note: make a change tells us the letters of the preceding words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone was posted elsewhere so as to give them a change of scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a change' rearranges INSTEAD and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier posted somewhere is stationed there, assigned to that place.

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, so take its first letter

parts.note: a castle is another name for the rook in chess

explanation.surface: A villain began his career at a Welsh fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: Caernarvon Castle is a famous medieval fortress in North Wales, but here 'Castle' is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A crook is a dishonest person, a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Jezebel and Ruth among the rest ?

parts.note: both appear in the Old Testament, abbreviated OT
they are women, so what belongs to them is hers

explanation.surface: Two biblical women are counted among the remaining people.
explanation.walkthrough: Jezebel and Ruth are Old Testament women, so 'OT' plus 'hers' describes them. 'among' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The others are the remaining people or things.

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric or material
rates are estimates or valuations, as in rating a property

explanation.surface: A budget cuts the costings for cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash flesh, so lacerates means wounds with cuts.

parts.note: sous are old French coins of small value

explanation.surface: Money is handed over to a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: John Philip Sousa was the American composer of marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Sousa wrote famous military marches, so he is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Seed and something more for bird

parts.note: a pip is the small seed of an apple or orange
'it' is the indefinable extra quality, that certain something more which makes a person special

explanation.surface: A feeder offers grain and something extra for a garden bird.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for 'sex appeal' or 'that certain something' was a popular 1920s idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The pipit is a small brown songbird of fields and moors.

definitions.meaning: a fielder's position near the batsman on the off side, used as 'a cricketer's place'
a unit scored in a game or match

explanation.definitionFit: It names a cricket fielding position and also a unit of scoring.

clue.text: Gold coin, possibly ? Nothing in the river

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word coin may be read in another arrangement

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A gold coin might be found at the bottom of a river, or maybe nothing is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns COIN into INOC, placed between OR and O. 'in the' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a great South American river flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Republic and kingdom are in revolt

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom

indicators.note: revolt suggests overturning, so the words are in and are are shaken up into a new order

explanation.surface: A republic and a monarchy both face uprisings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolt' rearranges ARE IN to make RAINE, after UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine was then a Soviet socialist republic and is now an independent state.

clue.text: Bob well content in the kitchen

parts.note: a bob was the old British shilling, abbreviated s
an inkwell holds ink, so ink is the content of a well

explanation.surface: A man called Bob is happy to stay in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name, and 'well content' like 'quite happy'. A bob was slang for a shilling, an old British coin worth one-twentieth of a pound, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: The basin for washing dishes is the thing found in every kitchen.

clue.text: " 'They told me, -, they told me you were dead" (Cory)

definitions.text: " 'They told me, -, they told me you were dead" (Cory)

parts.words: " 'They told me, -, they told me you were dead" (Cory)
parts.note: the opening line of William Cory's elegy for a Greek poet friend, the blank being the friend's name and the poem's title

explanation.walkthrough: William Cory's poem, a translation of Callimachus, begins 'They told me, Heraclitus, they told me you were dead'; the blank is the addressed name.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the name of the poet friend addressed in Cory's famous elegy.
